items.title: Lorraine Feather interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, March 22, 2023
items.q: So we did the album and we did some gigs together that were super fun.

ctx.x: Well no, not right now. And I miss Stephanie a great deal. Performing with her was just fantastic. We had a multi-media thing going that her late father had put together with lyrics on a screen and then there’s a little cam on Stephanie’s flying fingers. And we had a video and various pictures of James P. Johnson, Fats Waller. But that was a moment in time. We just became fans of each other through mutual friends and we got together —

we thought it would be good to do a gig and then we said well let’s do an album. And I had used up so many Fats Waller tunes on my own Fats album that we tried to concentrate on James P. Johnson. But Stephanie, who was — I always forget how old she is — but she looked like she was 12 at the time I was working with her, she was so young. But she knew all of this old James P. Johnson stuff and Willie “The Lion” Smith and some other composers I’d never heard of. There was a guy named Robin Frost who wrote something…
Wow. That’s sort of a specialized genre but over the years can you articulate what makes for a valuable piano accompanist?
